takeaway: Give 1 g IV tranexamic acid as soon as possible after postpartum haemorrhage starts: death due to bleeding fell from 1.9% to 1.5% overall and from 1.7% to 1.2% when treatment was within 3 hours [1].
clinicalQuestion: Does the timing of tranexamic acid change death from bleeding in postpartum haemorrhage?
background: Trauma data had already shown that tranexamic acid must be given early. WOMAN tested that question in postpartum haemorrhage [1].
population: Women with postpartum haemorrhage; 10,036 assigned tranexamic acid and 9,985 placebo were analysed.
intervention: 1 g IV tranexamic acid, with a second 1 g if bleeding continued after 30 minutes or restarted within 24 hours.
mainFindings: Death due to bleeding was 155/10,036 (1.5%) with tranexamic acid versus 191/9,985 (1.9%) with placebo (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.65–1.00; p=0.045). Within 3 hours of birth the figures were 1.2% versus 1.7% (RR 0.69, 95% CI 0.52–0.91; p=0.008). Hysterectomy was not reduced. The authors conclude the drug should be given as soon as possible after bleeding onset [1].
clinicalMeaning: Timing is part of the treatment. Waiting past the early window gives up the bleeding-death benefit seen in the trial [1].
limitations: The overall bleeding-death result was borderline (p=0.045). Hysterectomy did not fall. The within-3-hour analysis is a subgroup, prespecified in the sense that the trial emphasised early treatment [1].
bottomLine: Give 1 g IV as soon as postpartum haemorrhage is diagnosed, and do not expect the trial to show fewer hysterectomies [1].
practiceImplication: Do not delay the first dose for theatre or for a second uterotonic cycle if bleeding is already diagnosed [1].
safetyOutcomes: The trial report states no adverse effects offsetting the bleeding-death reduction.
trustRationale: Large international double-blind randomised trial with a prespecified emphasis on early treatment.
whatNotToOverclaim: Do not use a prevention meta-analysis as the source for treatment timing.
